questions.text: What is the worst case time complexity of inserting [latex]n^2[/latex] elements into an AVL-tree with n elements initially?
questions.solution:
Each AVL insertion costs [latex]O(\log N)[/latex], where N is the current size, at most [latex]n^2+n[/latex]. [latex]\log(n^2+n)=\Theta(\log n)[/latex].

[latex]n^2[/latex] insertions [latex]\times[/latex] [latex]\Theta(\log n)[/latex] = [latex]\Theta(n^2\log n)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n^2\log n)[/latex]

questions.text: Which one of the following regular expressions represents the set of all binary strings with an odd number of 1's?
questions.solution:
Check each option against strings with an odd number of 1s:
- Option 1: [latex](0+1)^*[/latex] inside can add extra 1s, e.g. 1111 (even) is generated False
- Option 2: always ends with 1, so "10" is missing False
- Option 3: always starts with 1, so "01" is missing False
- Option 4: [latex](0^*10^*10^*)^*10^*[/latex] gives pairs of 1s and then one more 1, but a leading 0 before a single 1 (e.g. "01") cannot be produced False

None of the options is exactly right, so the official key gave marks to all. A correct expression is [latex]0^*1(0^*10^*1)^*0^*[/latex].

Answer: Option 4 is the closest (MTA in the official key)

As per Official GATE CSE 2020 Answer key _MTA (Marks to All)

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.

I. If [latex]L_1\cup L_2[/latex] is regular, then both [latex]L_1 \; and \; L_2[/latex] must be regular.
II. The class of regular languages is closed under infinite union.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: take [latex]L_1[/latex] = any non-regular language and [latex]L_2=\Sigma^*[/latex]. The union is [latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] (regular), but [latex]L_1[/latex] is not [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: any language is an infinite union of single strings, each regular. If this were closed, every language would be regular [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Neither I nor II

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.

I. Symbol table is accessed only during lexical analysis and syntax analysis.
II. Compilers for programming languages that support recursion necessarily need heap storage for memory allocation in the run-time environment.
III. Errors violating the condition 'any variable must be declared before its use' are detected during syntax analysis.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: the symbol table is used in later phases too (semantic analysis, code generation) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: recursion needs a stack of activation records, not a heap [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- III: "declare before use" is a context-sensitive check done in semantic analysis [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: None of I, II and III

questions.text:
Consider the language [latex]L=\{a^n|n\geq 0\}\cup \{a^nb^n|n\geq 0\}[/latex] and the following statements.

I. L is deterministic context-free.
II. L is context-free but not deterministic context-free.
III. L is not LL(k) for any k.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- A DPDA can push a's and, on reading b's, pop them; it accepts if it is still on a's or the counts match. So L is deterministic CFL [latex]\text{---}[/latex] I TRUE, II FALSE.
- An LL(k) parser must decide at the start whether the string is [latex]a^n[/latex] or [latex]a^nb^n[/latex], but with long runs of a's, k symbols of lookahead are not enough [latex]\text{---}[/latex] III TRUE.

Answer: I and III only
